notesStmt.note: Based on Whitman's note, this manuscript was likely composed in 1890, sometime before or early in November. The envelope on the verso is also postmarked 1890. The envelope is glued to a portion of a letter by an unknown author, requesting an autograph.

This is seemingly the first page of a draft of a cluster of poems that was seemingly never published under this title. An extant proof slip of the cluster contains the poems "Sail out for good, Eidolon yacht!," "My task" (published as part of "L. of G.'s Purport"), "L. of G.'s Purport" (only the first two lines of the poem of the same title published in 1891), "Death dogs my steps" (published as part of "L. of G.'s Purport"), "For us two, reader dear," and "Grand is the seen." All of these poems were published, in some form, in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891). As Whitman's note on this manuscript states, he submitted the cluster to Arena magainze in November 1890 but it was rejected. He would later re-work the cluster and submit it, under the title "An Old Man's Recitatives," to Scribner's magazine on December 17, 1890, and it was again rejected.

lg.head: Sail out for good, Eidólon yacht!
lg.l:
O little white-hull'd sloop, now speed on
really deep waters,
(I will not call it our concluding voyage,

But outset and sure entrance to the truest,
best, maturest;)

Depart—depart from solid earth—no more
returning to these shores,

Now on for aye our infinite free venture
wending,

Spurning all yet tried ports, seas, hawsers,
densities, gravitation,
Sail out for good, eidólon yacht of me!
